subject: Dedicated deployment: certification for regional pinning & purge workflow
messages:
From: Alice Carroll <alice.carroll@fintechco.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: formal certification of pin & purge controls for Dedicated environment

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our security review for Dedicated hosting, our InfoSec team needs a short, formal statement and supporting evidence that describes exactly how Redwood: 

- Ensures a tenant can be pinned to a single geographic region (no active compute or storage replication outside the pinned region).
- Guarantees deletion/purge of tenant data (including snapshots and backups) within X days once a delete request is issued.
- Handles cross-region restore / disaster recovery scenarios (what triggers replication and how do you document it).

Could you provide a one-page certification and any artifact we can include in our vendor risk file (playbook, retention matrix, or sample audit log entries)? We also need to understand any exceptions (e.g., transient replication for maintenance) and the SLA for confirmations once a purge is complete.

Best,
Alice Carroll
Security Engineer, FinTechCo
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alice Carroll <alice.carroll@fintechco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: formal certification of pin & purge controls for Dedicated environment

Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Lauren (Director, Platform Security) for the certification doc and Grace (Product Ops) for the operational evidence (playbooks + retention matrix).

High-level answers up front: 
- Region pinning: we support customer-specified region binding at provisioning time; network and compute scheduling are constrained to pinned AZs and the storage layer is configured to use region-local buckets with tenant-scoped access controls.
- Purge timeline: our standard dedicated wipe workflow completes logical deletion within 24 hours and physical erasure of tenant-attached ephemeral storage and KV caches within 72 hours; backups and snapshots are retained per the customer-configured retention window — when a full-tenant erase is requested we trigger snapshot revocation and a retention-override purge that completes within 30 calendar days by default.
- Cross-region replication: not enabled for pinned tenants except in documented DR activations; any temporary replication for maintenance is logged and requires approval from our SRE on-call.

We will prepare: (1) a one-page certification statement, (2) the erase playbook with timestamps for each step, (3) a replication matrix showing allowed flows, and (4) sample audit log exports. Attached is an initial playbook and the replication matrix for your review — Lauren/Grace, please see the TODOs in the playbook.

Karthik
VP, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_erase_playbook_v2.pdf, replication_matrix_2026.xlsx
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alice Carroll <alice.carroll@fintechco.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: formal certification of pin & purge controls for Dedicated environment

Alice —

Quick tech clarifications to support the cert: 
1) Region binding is enforced at two layers: orchestration (scheduling constraints) and storage (S3 bucket policy + zone-local mount points). That prevents active writes/reads outside the region.
2) Snapshots: snapshot lifecycle is two-tier — short-lived ephemeral snapshots (used for fast node replacement) are retained for up to 7 days; durable customer-initiated snapshots are retained per customer policy. When a tenant erase request is processed we:
   • revoke snapshot access (immediate),
   • mark snapshots for purge and enqueue them for deletion (automated job),
   • run a verification job that attempts blind reads (no tenant keys) to confirm removal.
3) Backups: long-term backups are stored in region-local vaults by default. If customer elects cross-region replication for their own DR, that is a separately documented opt-in.
4) Exceptions: maintenance-driven cross-region replication (e.g., live migration for host evacuation) is extremely rare, and we require a change-control entry and timeline. We can provide a signed attestation log for such incidents if they occur.

Proposed next steps:
- We will draft the one-page cert that includes the standard timelines and a list of possible exceptions.
- Share sample audit log snippets (redacted) showing a completed purge workflow.
- If you prefer, run a joint tabletop/canary purge on a non-prod tenant and record the timestamps for the evidence file.

Grace — can you own the log export and schedule for the tabletop? Alice — would you like the canary run recorded and packaged as part of the artifact?

— Lauren
Director, Platform Security Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Carroll <alice.carroll@fintechco.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fintechco.com, security@fintechco.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: formal certification of pin & purge controls for Dedicated environment

Thanks — that level of detail is helpful. We would like: 
- The one-page certification (stamped and dated),
- The playbook and replication matrix (already attached),
- Redacted audit logs showing a completed purge.

A canary run would be ideal — please treat it as a non-prod tenant and let us know the proposed window. We prefer the audit artifacts to include the exact timestamps for each step in the wipe flow so we can match them to our vendor risk taxonomy. Also confirm: does the 30 calendar day purge window include any manual approval steps, or is it fully automated once we submit the erase request via the console/API?

Alice
FinTechCo
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Carroll <alice.carroll@fintechco.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: formal certification of pin & purge controls for Dedicated environment

Alice —

Thanks — we can schedule the canary purge for 2026-10-27 14:00 - 16:00 PT (non-prod tenant). The workflow is: 
1) Customer submits an erase request via Console or API (we record request ID).
2) System performs logical detach + access revocation (within 24 hours).
3) Snapshot revocation job marks assets for deletion (enqueue within 48 hours).
4) Physical erasure of ephemeral volumes and vault sweep completes by 72 hours for ephemeral and by 30 days for historical backups (purge job runs and then a verification sweep).

To answer your question: the standard 30-day purge for durable backups is automated once the erase request is submitted. Manual approvals are only required for out-of-band DR activations or when a customer has a custom retention contract that prevents immediate purge. We will include the exact Console/API request parameters and sample audit log snippets in the deliverable.

Deliverables we will send by 2026-10-22:
- Signed one-page certification (PDF),
- Redacted audit logs (CSV) for the canary run (after 10/27),
- The playbook and replication matrix (attached).

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Product Operations
Redwood Inference
